title: Normalize tokenizer metadata and provide chat-template fallbacks during model onboarding
creator: Marco Chen
description: During recent model onboarding runs we've observed subtle incompatibilities between tokenizer metadata and the chat/templates used by the console and SDKs. This ticket implements: (1) a normalization step that canonicalizes tokenizer metadata supplied by model packages (e.g., standardize special token names/ids, unify byte-level vs. unicode tokenization flags), and (2) a template compatibility shim and fallback generator that ensures chat templates map to a model's tokenizer constraints and publishes a safe default template when the provided template would break length accounting or special-token placement.
acceptance_criteria: All newly onboarded models pass a tokenizer metadata validation check before being listed in the catalog.

If a model's chat template is not compatible with its tokenizer (subtoken boundary or missing special token), the ingestion step generates a fallback template and records why the original was rejected.
Performance profile is published for the onboarded version and associated with the canonical tokenizer metadata so downstream cost/latency estimates use correct token counts.
Integration tests in the ingestion pipeline simulate a set of 10 representative prompts and confirm token counts match runtime tokenization for the canonized tokenizer.
No user-facing regressions in existing catalog models (backwards compatible behavior preserved).
design_notes: We will persist a canonical tokenizer metadata blob (tokenizer_meta_v1.json) in model catalog entries. This stops repeated heuristic parsing at runtime.
Canonical fields: model_max_length, special_tokens_map (name->id), added_tokens list, is_byte_level(boolean), uses_bpe(boolean), merges_version(optional).
Chat templates will be validated against special_tokens_map and an estimated tokenization test harness before publication.

Fallback generator strategy: minimal-safe-template — remove or replace unsupported placeholders and inject explicit special tokens (e.g., <|system|>, <|user|>) if tokenizer recognizes them; otherwise produce a plain-turn template with explicit separators that we guarantee won't split subtokens in meaningful places.

Trade-offs: normalization increases onboarding latency slightly (~2-4s per model) but reduces runtime errors and customer incidents. We chose ingestion-time cost over runtime guards to avoid per-request overhead.
implementation_plan: Add tokenizer_normalizer.py: parse tokenizer.json (HF-style or custom), map fields to canonical schema, run heuristics for ambiguous cases (e.g., missing pad token id -> infer as eos or -1).
Add chat_template_validator.py: takes canonical metadata + template, returns compatible|incompatible with reason codes and a suggested fallback template string.

Pipeline change: onboarding worker runs normalizer -> validator -> publish canonical metadata + template (original or fallback) -> trigger performance profile publisher with canonical tokenizer for accurate length estimates.
Unit tests for edge cases: models with 1) no special token names, 2) overlapping added_tokens, 3) byte-level true with unicode templates, 4) very small model_max_length (e.g., 128).
Create integration test harness that tokenizes example prompts using the onboarded tokenizer binary (or HF tokenizer shim) and asserts the catalog counts match runtime counts.
PRs: initial implementation (ingestion + tests) -> internal review -> add fallback UI flag for console (PM/Design review).
testing_plan: Unit tests covering parser and canonicalizer logic (target 95% branch coverage for new modules).
Integration tests in CI that run sample prompts through the onboarding worker and a small local tokenizer process to assert counts/placement of special tokens.
Staging canary with 10% of new model uploads routed to updated pipeline; manual verification of 5 recent model packages that previously failed tokenization checks.
Load test to ensure the ~2-4s added latency at onboarding scale (100 simultaneous uploads) is acceptable and does not cause worker timeouts.
Add golden test fixtures derived from a mix of open models (GPT-style, LLaMA-style, BERT-style) to verify fallback templates behave consistently.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal): enable for internal-only catalog models. Monitor ingestion errors and template fallback rate. (1 week)
Phase 2 (canary): enable for 10% of external onboarding flows. Surface a telemetry dashboard with rejection reasons and fallback usage. (2 weeks)
Phase 3 (full rollout): mark canonical tokenizer metadata as required for all new models and update docs + SDKs. Migrate past catalog entries lazily over a month.
If discovery: roll back to previous ingestion behavior and revert schema publish.
risks: False positives in incompatibility detection could cause unnecessary fallback templates and degrade chat UX. Mitigation: conservative validator and manual review flags for P0 models.
Onboarding latency increase could exacerbate spikes in model ingestion queue; mitigations include worker autoscaling and async post-publish verification for non-blocking checks where safe.
Edge-case tokenizers (vendor-provided proprietary format) may not parse; fallback: require a small metadata shim from vendor or mark as 'manual review'.
Incorrect canonicalization could produce wrong token counts and mis-published performance profiles (customer impact). Mitigation: integration tests and a short canary window with human verification.
